page: Microsoft Azure M176-88bds_4_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for memory-intensive enterprise applications and large in-memory databases. Hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V, the server is driven by dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processors operating at clock speeds up to 4.0 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The hardware allocation provides 88 vCPUs across 44 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives.

Memory capacity is the defining specification of this instance, delivering 3,892 GB of system RAM, which translates to 44.23 GB per core. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate exceptional throughput across memory subsystems, logging 419.61 GB/s in large-block read operations and 181.06 GB/s in write operations. Local storage consists of an integrated 8,590 GB SSD, pairing massive memory headroom with extensive high-speed ephemeral disk capacity. The configuration does not bundle discrete GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier execution in heavily parallelized workloads, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 94,306.2 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,601.0. Extended instruction throughput reached 116,490.66, and database operations achieved 34,697.66. While single-thread performance benchmarks register within moderate brackets, multi-threaded operations and cache-resident tasks exhibit superior scalability. Despite lacking dedicated GPUs, hardware matrix extensions facilitate respectable CPU-based inference speeds on smaller neural network models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M176-88bds_4_v3 consolidates substantial memory and multi-core processing into a single host, minimizing the architectural overhead, licensing fragmentation, and network latency inherent in distributed clusters. The server is suited for enterprise relational databases, SAP HANA, Redis caching layers, massive in-memory analytics, and data pipeline compilation.
